record.original_question: If a Seidel matrix S has rank n - 1, must there exist a 0-eigenvector of S whose entries are all ±1?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.36. If rank(S) = n − 1, then there exists an eigenvector of S corresponding to 0 that has only ±1 entries ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a simple graph on n vertices with adjacency matrix A(G). The Seidel matrix of G is the symmetric n×n matrix S = J_n − I_n − 2A(G), where J_n is the all-ones matrix and I_n is the identity matrix; equivalently, S has zero diagonal, entries −1 in positions corresponding to edges of G, and entries +1 in positions corresponding to non-edges.

Suppose that rank(S) = n − 1 (so the eigenvalue 0 of S has geometric multiplicity exactly 1). Must there exist an eigenvector of S corresponding to the eigenvalue 0 whose entries all lie in {+1, −1}?
artifact.status_search_result: The broader question of Haemers (whether every singular Seidel matrix has a ±1 vector in its nullspace) was answered negatively in 2021 by Akbari et al., who constructed infinite families of graphs whose singular Seidel matrices have integer null vectors with arbitrarily large entries. These counterexamples disprove the general statement, but it is not clearly documented whether the special case rank(S) = n − 1 (nullity exactly 1) is also refuted by their constructions; thus the restricted version stated here is at best partially settled.

status_evidence.title: On a question of Haemers regarding vectors in the nullspace of Seidel matrices
status_evidence.snippet: We construct infinite families of graphs which give a negative answer to this question. ... for every natural number N, there exists a graph whose Seidel matrix S is singular such that for any integer vector in the nullspace of S, the absolute value of any entry in this vector is more than N.
status_evidence.claim: Haemers' general question (singular Seidel matrix has a ±1 null vector) has been answered in the negative.

status_evidence.title: On a question of Haemers regarding vectors in the nullspace of Seidel matrices — ScienceDirect
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs infinite families giving a negative answer to Haemers' question and derives necessary conditions for singularity of Seidel matrices.
status_evidence.claim: Published version of the result disproving the general form of the conjecture.
